newsitem.title: CHILE: Peru, Ecuador leaders to hold a "friendly" meeting.
newsitem.headline: Peru, Ecuador leaders to hold a "friendly" meeting.

text.p: The presidents of Peru and Ecuador will meet in the Peruvian capital early next year for a "friendly meeting" that will not include talks on their countries' Amazon border dispute, they said on Saturday.

Exuding sunny goodwill and playing down the border row after a meeting in Chile, President Alberto Fujimori of Peru and Ecuador's Abdala Bucaram said they would discuss cooperation plans and maybe play a game of soccer in Lima.
"I think it will be a friendly meeting and a fervent show of two presidents looking for peace," Bucaram told reporters after meeting Fujimori at the Sixth Ibero-American Summit.
"The president (Fujimori) has invited me to Lima for the first half of January," he said.

"We're good friends, he's a good person, an intelligent man and he has done a lot for Peru," said Bucaram about Fujimori, in contrast to the animosity between the two nations early this year when shooting erupted on their jungle frontier.
Both presidents said Saturday's talks had centred on cooperation in irrigation and rural development, with little talk of the border dispute now under negotiation by the countries' foreign minister.
"We haven't discussed the issue. Today we've talked about cooperation... it was an agreeable meeting," said Fujimori.

Bucaram, known for his colourful style, said the two would together eat cebiche, a popular Peruvian marinated fish dish, and said, "I'm going to play a game of soccer, but I don't know if Alberto will too."
In talks in Chile last month, Peru and Ecuador agreed to open fullscale negotiations on the border dispute by the end of the year with the goal of reaching a final settlement.
